bridge_source.role: Exact bridge/materialization source for the current R-1 candidate. PR #34 head 31cbae12 (tree b5c19c19) on hardening/forge-eb2-face-down-20261007: the E-B2 manifested face-down construction (#561) plus the review P3 fix that chains the cause of a failed face-down placement, carried on the forge#33/forge#35 successor line. Ancestry: c3a025fa (E-B2 face-down construction) on 80336359 (the forge#33 G1 R1 merge, tree e5731fea); 6a1a60c5 adds the P3 cause chaining (throw new IllegalStateException("face-down placement failed", t)); the PR #34 head 31cbae12 (parents 6a1a60c5 and d9e356aa, tree 27bee40d) merges that branch back onto the forge#35 successor line. Over d9e356aa the only changed paths are forge-protocol2-bridge/: ScenarioBootstrap.java (0339d40d -> 5b722a18), StateProjection.java (b3f801c3 -> e9aa6e3e) and the bridge test G1R1TurnBeganBootstrapTest.java; 0 Rules-Core files and 0 card-data files. The forge#35 removal of .foundry/oc561-g1-r1-forge-20261006.yaml is retained, so the H4F Rules-Core drift guard admits the successor tree. The bridge parses face_down/face_down_type (missing kind, unsupported kind and attached placements are rejected), places a battlefield MANIFESTED permanent face down with the engine's own manifest state setup (GameState.java face-down precedent; the Original card state is recorded for the view refresh), verifies the requested face-down state after the post-untap hook, and projects face_down (public, CR 708.2) plus face_down_type only when the observer's shown name is not a redacted marker. rules_core_base_commit binds it back to the admitted #11/#12 candidate. Exact-head CI on 31cbae12: Test build run 37634912575 (push) completed success (Java 17 at 14:44:19Z, Java 21 at 14:43:14Z), and the iOS compatibility gate run 37634912612 (push) plus pull_request run 37634922406 completed success; the pull_request Test build run 37634922429 mirrors it. truth_boundary: B4-D is external_rules_engine evidence for real pinned XMage deck import, Commander construction/start, live state observation, current-priority decision/legal-action handoff, real priority passing, stale decision/action rejection, bounded submission-ready targetless/nonmodal action execution including a real Rograkh commander cast, an externally exportable monotonic bridge audit event stream with action/decision identity and pre/post state hashes, and explicit per-game XMage lifecycle cleanup/reuse. The audit stream covers real bridge/XMage lifecycle and externally controlled action boundaries; it is not claimed to be an exhaustive raw internal XMage GameEvent tap. Globally complete legal-action enumeration and action submission remain unproven because target, mode, choice and combat classes are incomplete. Mulligan, seed-control, replay and complete production game-loop coverage remain unproven. This is not win-rate evidence and does not make XMage a production-ready provider.
